sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Virginia pepperweed is a 20–90 cm annual or biennial native to North America, found in open and disturbed places. It differs from L. latifolium, a rhizomatous perennial that is generally much larger.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The basal leaves are spatulate and often deeply divided; stem leaves are narrower. The tiny white flowers usually have two stamens. The flattened, nearly round silicles are about 2.5–3.5 mm across and have a winged margin.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: Botanical references list the leaves and fruits as edible. This does not replace reliable identification or the usual precautions for wild plants.
